newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE: World market for September 17 - Robusta futures in London ended somewhat lower on arbitrage and light origin selling but the downside was supported by keen roaster demand. By the close, the benchmark November was $5 off at $1,525 a tonne. Volume was 3,284 lots with activities centered on switches. According to one trader, the firmness in the switches helped put some stability in the market.

Arabica futures in New York posted slight gains, with the exception of the spot September contract, which fell sharply in heavy speculative liquidation a day ahead of its expiry, trade sources said. Spot September slid 3.90 cents/lb to 112.20 cents, with the bulk of selling occurring during the last few minutes of trading. As a result, the September/December spread collapsed although its margin remained relatively steep 6.35 cents. Benchmark December futures rose half a cent on the day to close at 105.85 cents.

News that the US warehouse stocks of coffee fell in August to their lowest level in seven years failed to move the market as the numbers were in line with expectations. With new crop beans starting to flow from Central and South America, warehouse stocks are expected to build steadily during the next few months.

EL SALVADOR - Coffee production in El Salvador could be down by up to 6 per cent in the 1996/97 cycle to around 2.9 million quintals (1 quintal = 46 kgs), a leading coffee research group said. Rene Martinez, the manager of Procafe, said irregular rainfall might cause a dip of around 225,000 quintals from the output in 1995/96.

Western growing regions have been worst hit by inconsistent rainfall, with a shortage of water over the short summer to January and then an abundance in April, first affecting flowerings and then cherry development.
Sources at the Salvadoran Coffee Council said exports to last week from the 1995/96 cycle had totalled 2.9 million quintals.

HONDURAS - Green coffee exports from October through August reached 2.1 million 60-kg bags despite a sharp drop in exports in August, the Honduran Coffee Institute said. Exports in August were a mere 53,654 bags, a sign the country has depleted its stock of coffee from the 1995/96 harvest. The new harvest begins in October.

Honduras' monthly exports have fallen steadily since their March peak of 274,002 bags and the August figure is less than half the July exports of 129,536 bags. Germany, the United States and Japan remain the country's major destinations, although the Netherlands, Spain and South Korea gain in importance.

SINGAPORE - Coffee imports in May 1996 amounted to 51,802 bags, sharply down from last year's 100,000 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996 (January/May) up to 588,242 bags, down 28.6 per cent on last year's 824,329 bags. Total imports in 1995 reached 1.92 million bags compared to 2.85 million bags in 1994.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Vietnam (111,800 vs 391,500 bags) and Laos (23,700 vs 25,000 bags).

Coffee exports in May 1996 amounted to 89,857 bags, down from 144,871 bags exported in May 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/May 1996 up to 612,423 bags, 30.4 per cent less than the tonnage exported in the like period in 1995. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 1.86 million bags against 2.79 million bags in 1994.
Major countries of destination for green coffee in January/May 1996 were Algeria (83,300 vs 58,300 bags), Australia (51,400 vs 126,000 bags) and Malaysia (46,600 vs 53,500 bags).
